# `scripts/fp/world/`

[Index](index.md)

## `scripts/fp/world/collision_world.gd`

class_name `CollisionWorld` · extends `Node`

Analytic on-foot collision (slice A; no physics engine, D2): walkable ground height per point, blocking boxes and prop cylinders per tile, water. Buildings block with bodies made from the model's own geometry (body_shapes.gd, baked into body_table.gd), not the whole-lot AABB, so yards, lots and parks are walkable; construction-site parts, street props (lamp poles, bus shelters, benches, hydrants, trunks) and test boxes block too. Picking uses the full view.building_aabb(i). Every query looks at the 3x3 tiles around the point. Deterministic and headless-safe.

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `AP = preload("res://scripts/fp/asset_paths.gd")`
- `BS = preload("res://scripts/fp/player/body_shapes.gd")`
- `RB = preload("res://scripts/fp/world/riverbed.gd")`
- `GP = preload("res://scripts/fp/world/ground_profile.gd")`
- `TABLE = preload("res://scripts/fp/player/body_table.gd")`
- `SOFT_STEP = 0.03`: Interim soft step (A deliverable 1; remove once G1 raises WS.GROUND_Y): next to a tile whose surface is at GROUND_Y, a higher tile at most SOFT_STEP above it ramps down over its outer SOFT_BAND, so the 42 cm grass ledge does not trap a player who drops onto grass.
- `SOFT_BAND = 0.05`
- `LAMP_POLE_R = 0.008`: Lit straights bake their lamps into the road model (roads.py:138-139, 166-169): each pole stands LAMP_OUT outside its Bulb_* (the arm reaches toward the road), plus two small posts.
- `LAMP_OUT = 0.08`
- `LAMP_POST_R = 0.0035`
- `LAMP_POSTS = [Vector2(-0.4, -0.2), Vector2(0.4, 0.2)]`
- `BUS_STOP_PATHS = [ "res://models/props/bus_stop.glb", "res://models/real/props/bus_stop.glb", AP.BUS_SHE...`
- `PROC_STOP_OFFSET = 0.43`: CityView's procedural shelter (no model file) stands 0.43 from the road centre.
- `PROC_STOP_SIZE = Vector3(0.34, 0.21, 0.20)`
- `PROP_DIRS = ["res://models/real/props/", "res://models/props/"]`
- `BOX_PROPS = [ "bench", "picnic", "planter_box", "planter_long", "barrier", "utility_box", "aircon",...`: Street props by file name: trunks and lamp poles are thin cylinders, these are boxes, foliage does not block, anything else is a cylinder of its footprint within PROP_R_MIN..PROP_R_MAX.
- `SOFT_PROPS = ["tree_bush", "tree_fern"]`
- `LAMP_R = 0.15 * WS.M`
- `TRUNK_R = 0.25 * WS.M`
- `CAM_CYL_MIN = 0.2 * WS.M`: Camera arms treat cylinders this thick or more (trunks, not lamp poles) as solid.
- `PROP_R_MIN = 0.1 * WS.M`
- `PROP_R_MAX = 0.5 * WS.M`
- `ROUND_SLIDE = 0.45`: Walking head-on into a pole keeps this fraction of the speed, sliding round it.
- `META_CYL_TOP = 3.0 * WS.M`: Cylinders from a G1 `colliders` meta carry no height: they block up to this.
- `PERSON_R = 0.22 * WS.M`: A person on foot is a soft circle this wide (half a shoulder): the hero cannot walk through them, but they are not a wall either (soft_people_move; walkers.gd gives way in turn).
- `SOFT_RATE = 0.35`: How much of a person overlap the hero eases out per collision sub-step: gentle, so a sidewalk still flows; the into-person speed is damped player-side, so the overlap never persists.
- `SOFT_Y = 1.2 * WS.M`: A person's circle only presses the hero when their feet are within this height (a walker under a ledge the hero stands on is not in the way).
- `RESOLVE_STEP = 2.0 * WS.M`: resolve_out() moves at most this far per pass and makes at most this many passes, deepest face first: a teleport left inside a building steps straight out, a spawn deep inside never flings through walls.
- `RESOLVE_PASSES = 6`
- `GRADE_SURFACES = ["asphalt", "gravel", "dirt", "trail"]`: surface_at() on the carriageway of each road grade (D.ROAD_GRADES order).

### Properties

- `dynamic_boxes: Array[AABB]`: Boxes that move with the traffic (stopped cars from E's blockers_near), refreshed by the player a few times a second; they block like walls while listed.
- `people_circles`: People on foot near the hero, as soft circles the player refreshes every frame from traffic's walkers_near: (x, y, z, r) quadruples in world units. They are not walls (soft_people_move), but the hero cannot pass through them either.

### Functions

- `func setup(p_ctx: FpContext) -> void`: Stores the context; colliders are computed lazily from ctx.view.
- `func rebuild_all() -> void`: Drops every cached collider (after view.setup).
- `func invalidate(i: int) -> void`: Invalidates tile i's colliders: its holder changed (a street prop knocked down or put back).
- `func on_tile_built(i: int, _holder: Node3D) -> void`: Invalidates tile i's colliders.
- `func on_tile_cleared(i: int) -> void`: Invalidates tile i's colliders.
- `func add_test_box(b: AABB) -> void`: Test hook: a world box that blocks like any other (a ledge, a ceiling), listed in boxes() of every tile it overlaps.
- `func add_test_cylinder(x: float, z: float, r: float, top: float) -> void`: Test hook: a world cylinder (a trunk) at x, z of radius r up to top, listed in cylinders() of every tile it overlaps.
- `func clear_test_boxes() -> void`: Removes every add_test_box() box and add_test_cylinder() cylinder.
- `func tile_at(p: Vector3) -> int`: Tile index at a world point (round x/z, D.idx) or -1 outside the world.
- `func ground_height(p: Vector3) -> float`: World y of the walkable surface at p.x/p.z; NAN when not walkable (water, bridge parapet). With the ground_profile flag the lot slabs, pads and aprons are the exact steps and slopes of the meshes (GroundProfile); off, a lot is flat LOT_TOP across its whole tile.
- `func wade_height(p: Vector3, wade_max: float) -> float`: The bed height under p where the hero may wade (open water, not a bridge, at most wade_max deep), else NAN. Only the hero asks: ground_height() stays NAN over water, so NPCs, cars, animals and thrown bodies treat the river as the wall it always was.
- `func water_depth(p: Vector3) -> float`: How deep the open water is over the bed at p, in world units; 0 on land, on a bridge and on the dry part of a bank.
- `func walk_height(p: Vector3, wade_max: float = 0.0) -> float`: The height the feet stand at: ground_height(), with the interim soft step (SOFT_STEP ramps over SOFT_BAND toward a GROUND_Y neighbour) only when the ground_profile flag is off. NAN where ground_height is NAN, except for a wader (wade_max > 0): over open water no deeper than wade_max it is the riverbed.
- `func support_height(p: Vector3, radius: float, feet_y: float, max_rise: float, wade_max: float = 0.0) -> float`: What the feet of a walker at feet_y stand on at p: walk_height(), or the top of a box under the circle that is at most max_rise above the feet (a low wall it stepped or jumped onto). NAN over water, except the shallows for a wader (wade_max, see walk_height).
- `func surface_at(p: Vector3) -> String`: Surface name for footsteps and audio: "asphalt"|"sidewalk"|"lot"|"grass"|"dirt"|"water"|"bridge", or on the carriageway of an unpaved road "gravel"|"dirt"|"trail" (its verges are "grass").
- `func is_blocked(p: Vector3, radius: float, wade_max: float = 0.0) -> bool`: True if a circle of `radius` at p (feet) is blocked: unwalkable ground under p, or a box or a prop cylinder of the 3x3 tiles around p whose top is above p.y. Boxes are grown by radius in xz (a square, so it agrees with tests that grow AABBs).
- `func body_blocked(p: Vector3, radius: float, height: float, wade_max: float = 0.0) -> bool`: is_blocked() for a body `height` tall: boxes and cylinders entirely above p.y + height (an awning, a ceiling) let it pass.
- `func move_and_slide(from: Vector3, motion: Vector3, radius: float) -> Vector3`: Moves from `from` by `motion` (y ignored), sliding along blockers. S0 rules: try the full move, else x only, else z only, else stay; a player who already overlaps a box may take any of them that enters nothing new and goes no deeper. Returns the new feet position (y unchanged).
- `func move_body(from: Vector3, motion: Vector3, radius: float, height: float, max_rise: float, wade_max: float = 0.0) -> Vector3`: The walker's move: like move_and_slide() for a body `height` tall that can rise at most max_rise onto higher walkable ground (STEP_HEIGHT on foot, 0 in the air). A blocked move first slides along the contact (a pole's tangent, a wall's face), then along x or z alone. Returns the new feet position with y unchanged (the caller follows walk_height()). A wader (the hero, wade_max > 0) may also stand in water up to wade_max deep.
- `func soft_people_move(p: Vector3, radius: float, height: float, wade_max: float = 0.0) -> Vector3`: The hero's soft push out of the people circles at p, one nudge per collision sub-step (SOFT_RATE of each overlap): the point eased clear of everyone standing near, never through a hard blocker and never onto ground it could not stand on. Returns p unchanged when nobody overlaps. The walkers give way as well (walkers.gd), so a sidewalk keeps flowing.
- `func resolve_out(p: Vector3, radius: float, height: float, wade_max: float = 0.0) -> Vector3`: Pushes a body (radius, height) that sits inside blockers out to the nearest free side: a teleport or a load may leave it half inside a building or a car box, and the walk-out rule of move_body only helps once it moves. Deepest face first, at most RESOLVE_STEP a pass and RESOLVE_PASSES passes, and it stops the moment a pass makes things no shallower, so a body deep inside works its way out over a few steps instead of being flung through walls. Returns the pushed point (y unchanged); p itself when nothing overlaps or there was no way out.
- `func nearest_free(p: Vector3, radius: float, max_dist: float, wade_max: float = 0.0) -> Vector3`: The closest point to p (xz, y on the ground) where a circle of `radius` is not blocked, searched on rings 1 m apart out to max_dist; Vector3(NAN, NAN, NAN) when there is none.
- `func raycast(origin: Vector3, dir: Vector3, max_dist: float, include_props: bool = true) -> Dictionary`: Ray against each tile's pickable bounds (tile DDA, <= max_dist) and the ground: a building's full view.building_aabb(i) (kind "building", so a set-back house is still picked from the sidewalk), a site's parts (kind "building", the site tile), street props (kind "prop", when include_props) and the ground (kind "ground"). {"hit": bool, "pos": Vector3, "normal": Vector3, "tile": int, "kind": String, "dist": float}
- `func line_of_sight(a: Vector3, b: Vector3) -> bool`: True when the segment a -> b clears every movement box (bodies, walls, site parts, prop boxes) of the tiles it crosses; thin cylinders (poles, trunks) never hide anyone.
- `func sweep_sphere(origin: Vector3, dir: Vector3, max_dist: float, radius: float) -> float`: Free distance along unit dir from origin (<= max_dist) for a sphere of `radius`: a ray against the camera boxes near origin (camera_boxes_near) grown by radius (a Minkowski sum), skipping boxes that already contain origin. The camera arms (A 6.6, the drive and door cameras).
- `func camera_boxes_near(p: Vector3, reach: float) -> Array[AABB]`: boxes_near() plus every cylinder of CAM_CYL_MIN or more (tree trunks) as its square column: a camera must not end up inside a trunk, while lamp poles are thin enough to flash past. Parkour keeps boxes_near(), so trees are never vaulted.
- `func boxes_near(p: Vector3, reach: float, cyl_min: float = INF) -> Array[AABB]`: Movement boxes of the tiles around p within `reach` of it (the camera rig gathers them once per frame and sweeps the list several times), with the cylinders of radius cyl_min or more as square columns (none by default).
- `static func sweep_boxes(origin: Vector3, dir: Vector3, max_dist: float, radius: float, list: Array[AABB]) -> float`: sweep_sphere() over a given box list.
- `static func ray_box_t(origin: Vector3, dir: Vector3, b: AABB) -> float`: Entry distance of a ray (unit dir) into box b, or -1 on a miss (or when origin is inside).
- `func boxes(i: int) -> Array[AABB]`: Blocking boxes of tile i for movement, world space, cached until the tile is rebuilt (the cached array itself is returned: read it, never modify it): the building's bodies and walls (body_shapes.gd), every view.site_boxes(i) part (which can reach into neighbouring tiles), prop boxes (bus shelters, benches) and add_test_box() boxes overlapping the tile.
- `func body_boxes(i: int) -> Array[AABB]`: The building bodies of tile i (at most body_shapes.MAX_BODIES, inside view.building_aabb(i)).
- `func cylinders(i: int) -> PackedFloat32Array`: Prop and post cylinders of tile i as (x, z, r, top) quadruples in world space: lamp poles, trunks, hydrants, bins, the building's own posts.
- `func box(i: int) -> AABB`: Merged bound of boxes(i) (AABB() when none). Movement and tests use boxes(); interaction raycasts use the full view.building_aabb(i).

## `scripts/fp/world/ground_profile.gd`

class_name `GroundProfile` · extends `RefCounted`

The height of the ground under a point of a land tile, written once. The meshes that CityView and the street dressing build (the C/I pad, the rubble slab, the lot apron), the road and lot models authored in Blender (their heights are the WS constants, checked against the real meshes by tools/tests/fp_ground_profile_test.gd) and CollisionWorld.ground_height (which the hero's feet and everybody else's follow) all read the numbers here, so what the eye sees under the feet is what the feet stand on, and a step of the mesh is a step of the collision. Const-only and static: no state, no nodes, no randomness (the sim stays headless-safe). Local coordinates (lx, lz) are the offsets from the tile centre in tile units, -0.5 .. 0.5. Preload as GP, or use the class name. Lot slabs. A real building model (every zone R, C and I lot and every service building on foot) stands on its own slab, 8 cm high (WS.LOT_TOP) and 0.94 tile wide (WS.LOT_FOOTPRINT, half LOT_HALF); fresh rubble is a slightly wider slab (PAD_HALF, PAD_TOP), and so is the fallback pad of a stand-in model (within 1 cm of the slab's height, so the slab's number serves). The 0.03 tile (0.6 m) all round a slab is the lawn at GROUND_Y, so the slab edge is a step of LOT_TOP. Where the lot fronts a road, the apron (street_dressing.gd) climbs from the slab edge to the road's sidewalk over the last 0.03.

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `LOT_HALF = WS.LOT_FOOTPRINT * 0.5`: Half the width of a real lot slab (the model's own, authored 0.94 wide).
- `PAD_HALF = 0.48`: Half the width of the rubble slab and of a stand-in C/I model's pad (CityView builds them 0.96 wide).
- `TILE_HALF = 0.5`: The tile edge, where the road's sidewalk begins.
- `APRON_FROM = LOT_HALF`: The apron runs from the lot slab's edge to the tile edge, toward the road.
- `APRON_TO = TILE_HALF`
- `SIDES = [Vector2i(0, 1), Vector2i(1, 0), Vector2i(0, -1), Vector2i(-1, 0)]`: The sides an apron can lie on, as (dx, dy) toward the road (the order of the bits of apron_mask).

### Functions

- `static func slab_top(sim: CitySim, i: int) -> float`: The height of the slab of land tile i (a built lot, a service building's lot, rubble), or WS.GROUND_Y where the tile has none (open ground, a vacant lot, a construction site).
- `static func slab_half(sim: CitySim, i: int) -> float`: Half the width of the slab slab_top() describes: the rubble is a little wider than a real model's own slab.
- `static func apron_mask(sim: CitySim, i: int, frontage: int) -> int`: Which sides of tile i carry an apron, as bits in SIDES order: a built zone lot has one on the road it fronts (frontage, a road tile index or -1; every road side for a C/I lot), a service building's lot on every road side. 0 for tiles that are not a built lot.
- `static func apron_height(t: float) -> float`: The apron's height at distance t (tile units from the tile centre, toward the road): the slab edge's LOT_TOP at APRON_FROM, the sidewalk's SIDEWALK_TOP at APRON_TO.
- `static func tile_height(sim: CitySim, i: int, lx: float, lz: float, directory: CityDirectory = null) -> float`: The walkable surface height at local (lx, lz) of tile i: the road's own profile on a road tile (RoadTopology.surface_height), NAN over open water, else the slab of a lot, the lawn, and the aprons of a lot that fronts a road (directory, a CityDirectory, says which road a lot fronts; null: none). NAN means not walkable; the shallows of a river are the river bed's (riverbed.gd), which the CollisionWorld offers a wader.

## `scripts/fp/world/riverbed.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

The river-bed height, written once. CityView builds the bed mesh from node_height() and CollisionWorld lets the hero wade on tile_height(), which interpolates the mesh's own triangles, so what the eye sees under the water is what the feet stand on. Const-only: no state, no nodes, no randomness, so the sim stays headless-safe. Preload as RB. A water tile is a 4x4 grid of nodes at 0, BANK_W, 1 - BANK_W and 1 along each axis, split into 3x3 cells of two triangles each (a-b-c and a-c-d, a the corner nearest the tile's origin). A node sits at GROUND_Y where it touches land and sinks to RIVERBED_Y a bank's width inside the tile, so the banks are straight ramps of slope (GROUND_Y - RIVERBED_Y) / BANK_W (0.4 here, 22 degrees).

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `BANK_W = 0.2`: Bank width in tile units (4 m): the ramp from the grass down to the bed. A gentler shelf than the old 2 m, whose 0.8 slope no walker could climb (STEP_HEIGHT is 25 cm).
- `NODES = [0.0, BANK_W, 1.0 - BANK_W, 1.0]`: The node coordinates along each axis of a water tile.
- `CORNERS = [Vector2(0, 0), Vector2(1, 0), Vector2(1, 1), Vector2(0, 1)]`

### Functions

- `static func is_water_at(sim: CitySim, x: int, y: int) -> bool`: True for an in-world water tile. Outside the world counts as land (the bank closes the edge).
- `static func land_flags(sim: CitySim, x: int, y: int) -> Array[bool]`: Which of the eight neighbours of tile (x, y) are land: north, east, south, west (the edges), then the north-west, north-east, south-east and south-west corners (CORNERS order).
- `static func land_distance(land: Array[bool], gx: float, gy: float) -> float`: Distance (tile units) from the point (gx, gy) of a water tile, each 0..1 across the tile, to the land that touches it: an edge neighbour counts from its shared edge, a corner neighbour from the shared corner. 2.0 when no neighbour is land.
- `static func node_height(land: Array[bool], gx: float, gy: float) -> float`: The bed height at node (gx, gy): GROUND_Y at the land, RIVERBED_Y a bank's width away.
- `static func tile_height(land: Array[bool], lx: float, ly: float) -> float`: The bed height at (lx, ly) of a water tile, each 0..1 across it: the mesh's own triangle there.
- `static func bed_height(sim: CitySim, x: float, z: float) -> float`: The bed height under world point (x, z), or NAN when its tile is not water.
- `static func depth_at(sim: CitySim, x: float, z: float) -> float`: How deep the water is over the bed at world point (x, z), in world units: 0 on land and where the bed is above the surface (the dry part of a bank), WATER_Y - bed elsewhere.

## `scripts/fp/world/surface_feel.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

What each ground surface feels like to the hero (flag surface_feel), written once: the footstep set and its level and pitch, how much slower the surface is to run on, and how much dust a sprint kicks up. const-only and static, so tests pin every class. Preload as SF. The classes are CollisionWorld.surface_at's names, plus "sand" (the lawn and the dry shelf of a river bank inside the shore band, shore.gd: sand the ground shader paints there). The recorded step sets are asphalt, sidewalk, lot, grass, dirt, bridge and the splash set for water (sounds/fp, 33 KB each, nothing new is shipped); a class without its own recordings borrows the nearest and is told apart by level and pitch: sand   dirt, 3 dB soft and a fifth lower: a damp, dull scuff gravel dirt, 1.5 dB louder and a sixth higher: the grit of a crunch trail  grass, a little softer and lower: a worn path Speeds are factors of the top speed: pavement and slabs 1, a bridge 1, grass 0.98, a dirt track and gravel 0.97, trail 0.98, sand 0.93 (the softest). Dust, 0..1, is the share of the puff a sprinting step raises (0 on anything paved or wet).

### Constants

- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `RB = preload("res://scripts/fp/world/riverbed.gd")`
- `SHORE = preload("res://scripts/world/shore.gd")`
- `TABLE = { "asphalt": {"set": "asphalt", "gain": 0.0, "pitch": 1.0, "speed": 1.0, "dust": 0.0}, ...`: class -> {"set": footstep surface, "gain": dB on the step, "pitch": factor, "speed": factor, "dust": 0..1}.
- `FALLBACK = "sidewalk"`: The class of a surface name the table does not know: it sounds and runs like the sidewalk.
- `SHELF_M = 0.03`: A step on the dry shelf or the wet edge of a river (water shallower than this, m) is sand.
- `SAND_FROM = 0.5`: The sand's band of the shore, as a share of the shore band's own (shore.gd, 0..1 of its sand weight): from here on land counts as sand.
- `HL_SPEED = 0.2`: Top-speed factors ease toward their class with this halflife (s): no jolt at a surface edge.
- `DUST_MIN_MPS = 4.0`: A puff of dust needs the hero at least this fast (m/s): a run (4.5) or a sprint, not a walk.

### Functions

- `static func feel_at(col: CollisionWorld, surface: String, p: Vector3) -> String`: The feel class of CollisionWorld surface name `surface` at world point p: grass inside the shore band of a river and the dry shelf of its bank are "sand"; any other name is itself (an unknown one the FALLBACK).
- `static func near_water(sim: CitySim, p: Vector3) -> bool`: True when land point p lies in the sand of a shore: its tile touches water and its distance to the water is inside SAND_FROM of the band (shore.gd, which the ground shader paints).
- `static func row(c: String) -> Dictionary`: The row of class c (an unknown class gets FALLBACK's).
- `static func speed(c: String) -> float`: The top-speed factor of class c.
- `static func dust(c: String) -> float`: The dust share of class c.
- `static func step_set(c: String) -> String`: The footstep set (audio_bank.gd's SURFACES name) to play for class c.
- `static func street_wet(ctx: FpContext) -> float`: How wet the streets are, 0..1: the streetscape's weather, read by name (0 without it).
